Consequentialism holds that the rightness of an act depends solely on its outcomes. Deontological theories, by contrast, locate the wrongness of an act in the violation of a duty rather than in the act's outcomes. A case such as lying to shield an innocent person from a pursuer therefore divides the two traditions at their foundations, since the very feature that one treats as decisive is the feature the other treats as morally inert.

The controversy has a canonical text behind it. Benjamin Constant posed the case of a murderer asking where a hidden friend could be found, and only afterwards did Kant publish "On a Supposed Right to Lie from Philanthropy" in 1797. Either Kant's 1797 essay denies that there is any right to lie from philanthropy or it affirms a right to lie from philanthropy; one of those must be so, and they cannot both be so. Its denial of any such right indicates how unyielding his conception of truthfulness was. [1] That stance confirms the deontological diagnosis of wrongness given at the outset, on which what matters is the breach of duty and not what the act brings about. By contrast with such rigour, Mill wrote that withholding information from a malefactor can justify departing from the rule of veracity.

Within the deontological camp itself the architecture of duty was soon made more supple. W. D. Ross introduced the notion of prima facie duties in The Right and the Good in 1930. Ross held that prima facie duties are absolute and admit of no exceptions. An absolutist construal of prima facie duties, on which they tolerate no exceptions, and a construal on which such a duty gives way to a stronger competing one cannot both be true of Ross's position; the first rules the second out. A scholarly review of The Right and the Good determined that Ross's prima facie duties are defeasible, which shows that he held a prima facie duty can be overridden by a weightier competing duty.

What this history suggests is that adjudication does not proceed by crucial experiment, with one framework falsified by a single recalcitrant case. Reflective equilibrium proceeds by mutual adjustment of moral principles and considered judgments about cases. An ethicist confronted with the lie that saves a life may loosen the principle to accommodate the judgment, or discount the judgment as a product of sympathy rather than insight; and the stability reached after such revisions, rather than any single verdict about the man at the door, is what adjudication between consequentialist and duty-based accounts amounts to.

Adjudication between the institutional and the normative versions of the democratic peace has always been a quarrel about mechanism rather than about pattern, and the terms of that quarrel were fixed early. Michael Doyle revived the democratic peace thesis in a two-part 1983 article in Philosophy & Public Affairs, and that revival led directly to Bruce Russett's 1993 book "Grasping the Democratic Peace," which tested normative and structural explanations against each other. Everything since has depended on how the rival mechanisms are specified. Institutional accounts emphasize electoral accountability, legislative checks, and slow military mobilization as constraints on democratic leaders. Normative accounts emphasize the externalization of domestic habits of peaceful and tolerant conflict resolution.

Each mechanism can be restated as a claim about the actors whose conduct it purports to govern. The institutional constraint, that is to say, amounts to the proposition that democratic leaders face removal from office by voters for costly military failures; the normative mechanism, in other words, amounts to the proposition that democratic publics hold a normative aversion to using force against fellow democracies. [1] At least one of the two is at work in democratic dyads, electoral punishment for costly wars or popular distaste for striking fellow democracies, and perhaps both are.

The observational record is where the two accounts were first expected to part company. Either standard conflict datasets record zero interstate wars between two mature democracies, or they record at least one such war; exactly one of those tallies can be correct and not both, which is why the coding of regime thresholds and battle-death cutoffs has attracted such scrutiny. Even granting the null tally of wars between mature democracies, the inference from it to regime type has been resisted from outside the research program. Henry Farber and Joanne Gowa argued that the democratic peace is confined to the post-1945 era and reflects shared Cold War interests. Erik Gartzke's capitalist peace argument attributes the pattern to economic development, market institutions, and capital openness.

The mechanism-level literature has produced the sharpest tests of the two logics. Sebastian Rosato's 2003 article in the American Political Science Review argued that both the institutional and the normative causal mechanisms lack empirical support. Michael Tomz and Jessica Weeks found in survey experiments that American respondents were less supportive of military strikes against democratic targets. Rosato concluded that the institutional logic of democratic peace was validated and that only the normative logic failed. That conclusion and the verdict that neither the institutional nor the normative pathway finds empirical support cannot both be true, and the discrepancy has organized much of the subsequent reply literature. Tomz and Weeks found that respondents were equally willing to endorse strikes against democratic and nondemocratic targets, a result that cannot be squared with a reduced public appetite for force against democratic adversaries. The balance therefore now rests on individual-level evidence about accountability and aversion rather than on dyadic war counts alone.

The selection problem arises when unmeasured characteristics of residents determine which neighborhoods they live in.

It was precisely because the determinants of residential location remain unmeasured that the discipline turned toward designs resting on chance assignment. Unlike strategies that hold fixed whatever children of the same parents have in common, this newer approach seeks its leverage in variation imposed from outside the household. Randomized housing mobility experiments are designed to break the link between family characteristics and neighborhood context, and that design logic led researchers to use housing voucher lotteries as instrumental variables to identify neighborhood effects. A court confronted with two competing accounts of how an injury came about proceeds in two stages: it asks first whether the defendant's conduct is causally connected to the harm at all, and then whether some later act displaces that connection. The "but for" test asks whether the plaintiff's injury would have occurred absent the defendant's conduct. The "but for" test requires the plaintiff to prove that the defendant's conduct was the sole cause of the injury. An inquiry satisfied by showing that the harm would not have come about but for what the defendant did, and a demand for proof that nothing else contributed to the harm, cannot both state the same threshold of causal responsibility; the one formulation excludes the other. The plaintiff bears the burden of proving causation by a preponderance of the evidence. The defendant bears the burden of disproving causation in an ordinary negligence action. Placing the risk of non-persuasion on the injured party and placing on the party sued the task of dispelling the causal link cannot both describe the ordinary negligence action; the allocation cannot run in both directions at once.

[1] An intervening criminal act by a third party supersedes the defendant's negligence as a matter of law in every case. Treating predictability as the touchstone of supersession cannot be squared with a categorical severance of liability whenever the intervening act happens to be criminal, however predictable that crime may have been. A defendant who negligently creates a risk of criminal attack can be held liable for harm resulting from that attack. Automatic supersession in every instance of third-party crime rules out any liability founded on having negligently exposed the plaintiff to precisely such a crime.

Where the proof supports the second account, the third party's act broke the chain of causation between the defendant's negligence and the plaintiff's injury; that is to say, the intervening act operated as a superseding cause that cut off the defendant's liability for the injury. Whereas the defendant who negligently invites a criminal attack answers in damages for its consequences, the defendant whose negligence is displaced by a superseding intervention answers for nothing at all.

Causation is ordinarily a question of fact reserved for the jury, and it is for that reason that expert testimony is commonly admitted to establish the mechanism of the plaintiff's injury. Even though causation is thus the jury's province as a rule, a directed verdict on causation is appropriate when the evidence permits only one reasonable conclusion. Accordingly, where the record will bear only the defendant's conduct or only the intervening act as the operative cause of the harm, the court may resolve the question itself rather than submit it.

Adjudicating between inheritance and contact is a matter of asking which mechanism could have produced the particular shared feature, and the diagnostics available differ in kind. The comparative method establishes genetic relationship through systematic sound correspondences across the lexicons of two languages. Antoine Meillet, by contrast, treated shared morphological irregularities as the strongest evidence of common descent, since arbitrary paradigmatic anomalies are not the sort of thing a borrowing speech community reproduces wholesale. A further diagnostic concerns the internal stratification of the lexicon. [1]

The signature of contact cuts against the very regularity of correspondence on which the comparative method relies. Loanwords frequently violate the regular sound laws of the recipient language, and this irregularity is what makes it possible to date them relative to the sound changes they underwent or escaped. Structural resemblance poses a harder problem, because what diffuses in that domain is pattern rather than substance. Structural features such as vowel harmony and verb-final word order spread readily through language contact. Hungarian is a member of the Turkic language family.

The Hungarian case shows how such a dispute is settled on the evidence. Hungarian shares inherited basic vocabulary and verbal morphology with Khanty and Mansi, a correspondence that cannot be squared with membership in the Turkic family and that demonstrates instead that Hungarian belongs to the Uralic language family. That Uralic affiliation is itself the evidence indicating that every Turkic-looking word in Hungarian entered the language through borrowing. Only two outcomes are open here, and exactly one of them can hold: either every Turkic-looking item in the Hungarian lexicon is a loan, or at least one Turkic–Hungarian lexical resemblance is an inheritance from a common ancestor.

Within the borrowed stratum the chronology can be stratified further. At least one of the following is true, and perhaps both: some Turkic words entered Hungarian before the Magyars reached the Carpathian Basin, and some Turkic words entered Hungarian after the Magyars settled in the Carpathian Basin. The decision, in short, rests not on the bare existence of resemblance but on where in the lexicon the resemblance falls, whether it conforms to the sound laws of the recipient language, and whether it reaches into morphological paradigms.

Apportioning responsibility for an injurious contact between a collaborative robot and a human worker begins with an exact reconstruction of the cell as it stood at the moment of the event, since the engineering record, and not the parties' narratives, fixes both the mode of operation and the protective measures then in force. The collaborative robot was operating in a power and force limiting mode at the time of the contact. A safety laser scanner defined the protective field surrounding the robot's workspace. The applicable performance criterion must be stated with equal care: ISO/TS 15066 prohibits any physical contact between a collaborative robot and a human worker, and such a blanket prohibition cannot be squared with the force-limited mode under which the machine was running when the worker was struck, so the prohibition and that mode of operation cannot both stand.

Because ISO 10218-2 governs the integration, installation, and commissioning of a robot system within a workcell, a task-based risk assessment of the workcell was required before the robot was placed into production. Collaborative robot applications are exempt from the risk assessment requirements of ISO 12100, and that exemption cannot be reconciled with the pre-production assessment obligation just described; one or the other must give way, for both cannot be true of the same installation.

The manufacturer attributed the incident to the plant's alteration of the robot's safety configuration. The plant operator attributed the incident to a defect in the robot's force-monitoring firmware. Adjudication therefore depends on artifacts that survive the event rather than on either party's reconstruction of it. Firmware version records identify which software release was executing at the moment of contact. Checksum comparison of the stored safety configuration file reveals unauthorized parameter changes. Logged firmware identifiers, configuration checksums, safety-signal traces and maintenance records together allow the investigator to distinguish what the control software did from what the integrator and the maintenance crew did to the cell around it.

At least one of two failures is thereby established, and perhaps both: the robot's control software failed to limit contact force to the configured threshold, or the workcell installation deviated from the manufacturer's integration requirements. Even though the plant locates the origin of the event in defective force-monitoring firmware, the unauthorized parameter changes exposed by the comparison of configuration checksums are what demonstrate the second of these, namely the departure of the as-built cell from the integration requirements specified by the manufacturer. The protective stop did not activate before the worker was struck; in other words, the robot failed to halt its motion prior to making contact with the worker, and that failure to halt was brought about by the installation's deviation from the manufacturer's integration requirements. [1]

The practical consequence for such disputes is that neither attribution can be credited on its own terms. Only the physical and digital residue of the cell at the moment of contact, read against the integration duties that the standards impose on whoever commissioned the application, determines whether the fault lies in the sensing and control chain or in the practices that surrounded it.

Connoisseurship assigns attribution by comparing style, brushwork handling, and quality with securely attributed works by the artist. By contrast, radiocarbon dating of canvas fibres pinpoints the year of a painting's execution to within a single year. Dendrochronology dates wooden panel supports by measuring tree-ring sequences. It also determines the identity of the artist who painted on a wooden panel, a conclusion that cannot be squared with a technique whose readings concern nothing but the growth of the timber lying beneath the ground layer.

Stylistic judgement and documentary history are at best congruent with an attribution, whereas a material anachronism is decisive against one: no account of a master's hand can accommodate a substance that did not exist in his lifetime. Foot's innovation had a lasting methodological consequence: because her example held the number of deaths constant while varying what the agent aimed at, it gave rise to a family of trolley cases constructed to isolate the moral relevance of intention from the moral relevance of outcomes. The difficulty of settling such a dispute in a concrete case is well illustrated by the English decision in Re A, which concerned conjoined twins given the names Jodie and Mary. Adjudication between rival accounts of a practice shared by two distant societies begins from a methodological hazard that comparative anthropology has long recognized. Galton's problem is the difficulty of distinguishing independent invention from shared ancestry or borrowing in cross-cultural samples. Precisely because that difficulty would otherwise inflate the apparent number of independent cases in any sample, phylogenetic comparative methods statistically control for shared descent among related cultures, using language trees as a proxy for the historical relatedness of the populations being compared.

The pedigree of the objection is worth stating with care. Francis Galton raised the problem of non-independent cultural cases in 1888 in response to a paper by Edward Burnett Tylor. Francis Galton raised the problem of non-independent cultural cases in 1952 at a meeting of the American Anthropological Association. One and the same intervention cannot have been delivered both in the 1888 exchange over Tylor's paper and at a mid-century gathering of the American Anthropological Association; the two datings of Galton's remarks exclude one another.

The first of the rival accounts makes a definite historical claim about the two traditions. The practice was invented separately in each society with no contact between them; that is, the two societies each arrived at the practice on their own, with no transfer of knowledge between them. Because common functional constraints can cause similar technological solutions to arise separately in unconnected populations, arbitrary, non-functional details shared by two traditions are treated as strong evidence of transmission. Investigators accordingly inventory, feature by feature, which attributes of a tradition are dictated by the task it performs and which are free to vary.

Chronology supplies a second line of argument, and its limits must be specified. Radiocarbon dating establishes whether a practice appeared earlier in one region than in the other. Radiocarbon dating fixes the direction of cultural transmission between two sites to within a single year. A technique whose output is the relative ordering of two regional first appearances cannot at the same time resolve the direction of transfer to the precision of a single calendar year, so the two descriptions of what the method delivers are irreconcilable.

The Pacific sweet potato case shows how such reasoning is brought to bear on a concrete dispute. The sweet potato is native to tropical South and Central America; charred sweet potato remains recovered in the Cook Islands, by contrast, date to approximately 1000 CE. [1] Those excavated Cook Islands specimens demonstrate that Polynesians and Indigenous South Americans were in contact before 1500 CE, and the resemblance between the Polynesian word "kumara" for sweet potato and the Quechua word "kumar" independently confirms that such contact occurred. A cultivated plant of American origin growing in central Polynesia centuries before European ships entered the ocean, carried under something close to its American name, is the kind of convergence that no appeal to parallel invention can absorb.

Adjudicating between an observational failure and a failure of model physics after an unforecast tornado outbreak requires that the forecast record, the analysis fields and the behaviour of the parameterizations each be reconstructed and tested against the other two. The highest categorical risk level in a Storm Prediction Center convective outlook is "moderate", and the distance between the issued categorical designation and the observed severity fixes the magnitude of what has to be explained.

The human cost establishes the gravity of the review: either no one was killed during the tornado outbreak, or twenty-two people were killed during it; one of those two descriptions is the correct one, and no reconstruction can hold both at once. [1] The National Weather Service conducts formal service assessments after high-impact weather events, and such an assessment gathers the observing-network record, the assimilation diagnostics and the parameterization inventory into a single evidentiary file.

Routine upper-air radiosonde launches in the United States occur twice daily at 00 and 12 UTC, and that thin fixed cadence is what led to the provision under which forecasters request special off-hour radiosonde launches ahead of anticipated severe weather. Operational radiosondes are launched every three hours at every United States upper-air site; a uniform three-hourly ascent schedule and a fixed pair of launches at 00 and 12 UTC cannot both describe the same network, so one of the two characterizations has to be discarded before the observational record is interpreted at all. Because forecasters are in a position to call for those off-hour ascents, data assimilation blends observations with a background forecast to produce model initial conditions, and that blended analysis is the object any post-event diagnosis must interrogate first.

Two candidate culprits are then isolated, and at least one of them held during the event, perhaps both: the low-level moisture field in the model analysis was initialized too dry, and the boundary layer scheme mixed the near-surface layer too deeply during the forecast period. Observing System Experiments rerun a forecast with selected observations deliberately withheld, and those controlled reruns demonstrate that the missed forecast originated in the model's initial conditions rather than in its physical parameterizations. The resolution of that conflict determines whether the corrective action is an upgrade to the observing and assimilation chain or a revision of the scheme itself, and the service assessment states which of the two it endorses.

The first branch point in such a workup is biochemical. Transferrin saturation above 45 percent is a standard threshold for suspecting iron overload, while a transferrin saturation below 20 percent confirms a diagnosis of hereditary haemochromatosis; these two cut-offs cannot both be true, and the clinician must settle which one actually governs the interpretation of the patient's iron studies.

Because C282Y homozygosity is the most common genotype underlying hereditary haemochromatosis in people of northern European ancestry, HFE genotyping tests specifically for the C282Y and H63D variants. Either the patient's HFE genotype included at least one copy of the C282Y variant, or the genotype included no copy of the C282Y variant; one of these outcomes must obtain and both cannot, and the subsequent reasoning follows whichever one the laboratory reports.

Adjudicating between the supply-shock and the monetary-policy accounts of the 1970s turns on timing, on cross-country comparison, and on the estimated behaviour of the central bank's reaction function. OPEC imposed an oil embargo on the United States in October 1973. The price of crude oil, which can be traced through posted contract terms, roughly quadrupled between 1973 and early 1974. Hamilton, working through the postwar US record, documented a statistical relationship between oil price increases and recessions. [1] That recession regularity indicates that oil supply shocks account for the entire rise in US inflation during the 1970s.

The chronology, however, disciplines any such attribution. Only two descriptions of the pre-embargo record are available, and exactly one of them can be correct: either US consumer price inflation exceeded 5 percent before the October 1973 oil embargo, or it remained below 5 percent until that embargo. The published price indices place the decade in the first case, and inflation already above 5 percent in advance of the embargo cannot be squared with the view that oil supply shocks produced the whole of the decade's inflation. What can be affirmed is that at least one of two impulses was in operation, and perhaps both were: OPEC production cuts sharply raised the real price of crude oil in 1973 and 1974, and US money growth accelerated in the years preceding 1973.

The monetary side of the ledger rests on further evidence. Japan experienced lower consumer price inflation than the United States in 1974. The Federal Reserve's policy interest rate stood below the rate of inflation for much of the 1970s; in other words, real policy interest rates in the United States were negative during much of the decade, and the Japanese comparison for 1974 is precisely the sort of international evidence that shows those American real rates to have been negative. That sustained shortfall of real rates below zero is in turn evidence for the estimate of Clarida, Gali and Gertler that the pre-1979 Federal Reserve policy rule violated the Taylor principle: a central bank that raises its nominal rate by less than one-for-one with inflation will let real rates fall as prices accelerate.

The dispute was settled less by any single regression than by an institutional experiment at the close of the decade. Paul Volcker became chairman of the Federal Reserve in August 1979, and his arrival led to a tightening that pushed the federal funds rate above 19 percent in 1981. The lesson drawn from that episode is that a determined central bank can end an inflation whose proximate trigger lay in commodity markets, and the weight of professional judgment shifted accordingly toward the monetary account.

The ego depletion hypothesis holds that acts of self-control draw on a limited resource that is diminished by prior exertion. [1] The candidate accounts are familiar ones: the original effect was inflated by selective reporting, the replication's procedure was inert, the phenomenon is real but confined to conditions the replication did not reproduce, or the phenomenon does not exist at any appreciable scale. Baumeister, Bratslavsky, Muraven, and Tice published the original ego depletion experiments in 1998. Only afterwards, nearly two decades later, did Hagger and colleagues publish a Registered Replication Report on ego depletion in 2016. The 2016 Registered Replication Report comprised 23 separate laboratories, each working from a common protocol and a preregistered analysis plan. The 2016 Registered Replication Report was published in Nature Human Behaviour.

The pooled effect size in the 2016 multi-laboratory replication was d = 0.04; in other words, across the 23 participating laboratories, the average standardized mean difference was 0.04. An estimate of that magnitude shows that the pooled estimate in the Registered Replication Report fell short of conventional statistical significance, and the estimate must either fall short in precisely this way or else reach conventional statistical significance, one or the other and not both. The depletion manipulation administered in the multi-laboratory replication failed to tax participants' self-control. The dispute at the centre of contemporary metaethics can be stated in a sentence. Moral realism holds that moral judgments describe objective moral facts; expressivism, by contrast, holds that moral judgments express the speaker's non-cognitive attitudes. Shorn of its technical apparatus, the realist thesis is simply that moral judgments report facts about the world, and the terms of the disagreement ensure that at least one of that thesis and the competing claim that moral judgments express the attitudes of the speaker who utters them must be correct, perhaps both together. Adjudication therefore turns on which side can accommodate everything that moral language is observed to do.

Most of the pressure on the expressivist side arises from its semantic commitments. Since expressivism construes a moral verdict as the voicing of an attitude rather than the description of a state of affairs, it issues in non-cognitivism, which denies that moral sentences are truth-apt; in other words, on non-cognitivism moral utterances are incapable of being either true or false. That very incapacity generated the best-known objection to the programme. The Frege-Geach problem presses expressivists to explain the behaviour of moral terms embedded in conditionals, and that pressure led Simon Blackburn to develop quasi-realism to account for the apparently factual surface of moral discourse.

The realist camp has a repertoire of tests of its own, directed at the semantics of moral predicates rather than at the logic of embedded moral claims. G.E. [1] Neither tradition, however, yields a verdict from the armchair. Where the question is answered at all, it is answered about particular utterances in particular settings, by asking whether the words as used were verifiable, how a reasonable audience would have taken them, and what the surrounding context implied.

What settled the question was thus not the label borne by the utterance but its content: a sentence that purports to say how things stood is fact-stating, however it is dressed.

Serum procalcitonin, by contrast, is typically elevated in bacterial sepsis and low in drug hypersensitivity. A skin biopsy showing interface dermatitis with eosinophils supports a drug-induced etiology, which confirms that an adverse reaction to an administered drug caused the deterioration.

The suspect antibiotic was stopped on the day the patient deteriorated. Improvement after withdrawal of a suspect medication constitutes a positive dechallenge. Negative blood cultures definitively exclude bacterial infection as a cause of deterioration, a conclusion that cannot be squared with the capacity of broad-range 16S ribosomal RNA PCR on autopsy tissue to identify bacteria when cultures are sterile. The post-mortem examination came later, after that antibiotic had been withdrawn, and its result takes one of two forms: either the autopsy identified an infectious cause of death, or the autopsy found no infectious cause of death, one of the two being so and not the other.

Where molecular and histological results diverge from the clinical impression, the convention is to grade each strand of evidence by its specificity rather than to average them, since a finding that only one explanation can generate outweighs several that both explanations can produce. Causality assessment instruments formalize this by scoring temporal plausibility, competing causes, and the response to withdrawal and re-exposure, while the pathologist's report records what tissue can and cannot establish. The adjudicated verdict is then entered in the record together with its grounds, so that any later reader can identify the single observation that decided the case.

The quarrel over the Dark Ages was settled less by a single verdict than by a long reworking of the question, and its terms were set by Henri Pirenne. Pirenne attributed the rupture of Mediterranean trade networks to Arab expansion in the seventh century. His thesis held that the Germanic invasions of the fifth century ended Mediterranean economic unity, and these two datings of the break cannot both be true: a fifth-century terminus for Mediterranean unity rules out a terminus falling two hundred years later with the Arab conquests. Only after that thesis had been fully laid out did a second line of argument enter the field. Several historians argued that the apparent post-Roman decline reflected the loss of written sources rather than material impoverishment. Peter Brown popularised the concept of "Late Antiquity" as a period of cultural transformation. Academic historians now largely avoid the label "Dark Ages" in scholarly writing. [1]

The documentary question is in part a matter of simple survival. At least one of two things holds, and perhaps both: the production of written documents declined in the post-Roman West, or large numbers of early medieval documents were destroyed in later centuries. Because the texts could not therefore be made to answer for themselves, the challenge mounted by those historians led directly to the adoption of methods that bypassed texts altogether, and radiocarbon dating allowed early medieval settlements to be dated without reference to written records. [2]

Once material proxies entered the argument, the picture ceased to be uniform. Catalogued counts of Mediterranean shipwrecks fall sharply for the centuries after the fifth century; by contrast, Greenland ice cores show that lead pollution reached its ancient peak during the eighth century. Series of this kind measure different things, exchange in the one case and metallurgy in the other, and the discipline learned to weigh them separately rather than to assemble them into a single index of decline.

The Justinianic plague reached Constantinople in 541 CE, and the mortality it unleashed brought about the woodland regeneration that pollen sequences show across parts of post-Roman Britain. Dendrochronology supplies the chronological anchor, and here the evidence admits of exactly one of two readings: either European tree-ring sequences record sharply reduced growth in the 540s CE, that downturn being registered before the epidemic reached the imperial capital, or no tree-ring sequence records a growth downturn in the 540s CE at all. One of these two must hold of the rings, and they cannot both hold together. On the first reading the environmental and epidemiological records interlock closely, and it is that interlocking, rather than the silence of the chronicles, on which the modern verdict rests.

The failed unit was a 230/69 kV oil-immersed power transformer at the utility's substation. Two incompatible accounts of the event were placed on the record by the parties. The utility attributed the failure to a defect in the high-voltage winding insulation, whereas the manufacturer attributed the failure to a switching transient produced by capacitor bank operation on the adjacent feeder. Resolving a dispute of this kind is a matter of ordering the physical evidence, since the diagnostic signatures of an internally initiated fault and of an externally imposed overvoltage differ in kind. Engineers therefore begin not with the parties' assertions but with the records that the apparatus and its protection scheme generated independently of either of them.

Dissolved gas analysis measures fault gases dissolved in transformer insulating oil. [1] Applied to oil drawn from the failed unit, that measurement is what produced the central laboratory finding of the investigation. The dissolved gas analysis showed 480 ppm of acetylene in the oil sample, a reading that confirms the rule that elevated acetylene concentrations in insulating oil indicate high-energy arcing.

By contrast, elevated carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide levels in the oil indicate degradation of cellulose paper insulation, a signature that implicates the solid rather than the liquid portion of the insulation system. Digital fault recorders at the substation captured voltage and current waveforms during the event. Such records permit the sequence of voltage collapse and current rise to be reconstructed at sub-cycle resolution, which is the only way to establish whether the disturbance on the system preceded the collapse of dielectric strength in the apparatus or followed it. The surge arrester discharge counter at the transformer terminals registered the number of surge operations. Surge arresters eliminate all transient overvoltages at transformer terminals.

After the waveform records had been secured, untanking and internal inspection located the failure site within the winding, precisely the region that the elevated carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide readings had indicated. The geometry of the damage then becomes decisive: a puncture concentrated at the line-end turns, where impulse stress accumulates, carries a different implication from a failure distributed through the body of the coil. Taken together, the oil chemistry, the recorded waveforms, the surge history at the terminals and the physical condition of the conductor and paper permit the investigator to determine which of the two competing accounts the hardware itself will support, and to discard the other.

One further matter conditions the commercial consequences of whatever technical finding is reached. Either the transformer was within its manufacturer warranty period on the date of failure, or the manufacturer's warranty had expired before the date of failure; one of those two situations must be the case, and they cannot both obtain.
